title: Material Intake, Storage and Reclaim Practices and Processes

lessons.title: Your workplace experience at intake and stores
lessons.html:
Your workplace experience at intake and stores

This workplace module is completed on the job, under a mentor or supervisor. You must show that you can do intake, storage and reclaim work regularly and correctly in a real feed mill, and you must collect evidence in your logbook or portfolio.

What you should be exposed to

  • Receiving bulk grain and oilcakes by truck, and where applicable by rail.
  • Receiving bagged materials: premixes, minerals, vitamins, medicaments.
  • Receiving liquids: molasses, oil, fat.
  • Weighbridge operation and documentation.
  • Sampling, quick tests and handing samples to the laboratory.
  • Off-loading, routing to silos and bins, magnets and scalpers.
  • Silo monitoring, aeration and storage hygiene.
  • Warehouse stock control and FIFO or FEFO.
  • Reclaim to production bins.
  • Pest control programme and housekeeping.

Working with your mentor

  1. Agree a schedule of tasks and the evidence required for each.
  2. Watch the task being done, then do it under supervision, then do it on your own while observed.
  3. Ask questions about the reasons behind each step, not only the steps.
  4. Get each task signed off when you are competent.

Evidence for your logbook

EvidenceExample
Completed recordsGoods received notes, sample labels, silo temperature logs (copies or references)
Observation reportsMentor signs that you sampled a load correctly
Incident or problem reportsHow you handled a rejected load or a choke
Reflection notesWhat you learned and what you would do differently

Do not copy confidential supplier prices or company information into your portfolio; ask your mentor what may be included.

lessons.title: Standard practices you must demonstrate
lessons.html:
Standard practices you must demonstrate

Intake practice

  • Check documents and vehicle before weighing.
  • Sample according to the sampling plan, at several points and depths.
  • Recognise reject signs: musty smell, heating, live insects, wet grain, foreign material, treated seed.
  • Off-load only after acceptance, into the correct pit, with the route confirmed.
  • Complete weigh-in, weigh-out and goods received records accurately.

Storage practice

  • Keep bins and silos allocated and labelled; never mix materials.
  • Monitor and record silo levels and temperatures; report rising trends.
  • Operate aeration as instructed.
  • Keep bagged stock on pallets, within stack limits, FIFO or FEFO, with quarantine stock tagged.
  • Keep areas clean and report pest activity.

Reclaim practice

  • Confirm the request, source and destination.
  • Start routes downstream first and stop upstream first.
  • Monitor levels to prevent overfilling.
  • Record every transfer.

Safety behaviours your mentor will look for

  • Correct PPE every time.
  • Lockout before clearing chokes or opening covers.
  • Never entering silos, bins or pits without a permit and standby person.
  • Keeping clear of reversing and tipping trucks.
  • Good housekeeping to control dust.
  • Reporting hazards and near misses.

Handling a real problem

During your workplace time you will likely meet problems: a load that fails moisture, an elevator choke, a silo heating up. Record what happened, what you did, who you informed and what the outcome was. These real cases are some of the best evidence of competence.

Key points

  • This module is completed on the job with a mentor and logbook.
  • Observe, practise under supervision, then perform independently.
  • Demonstrate correct intake, storage and reclaim practice.
  • Show safe behaviour: PPE, lockout, permits, truck safety.
  • Record real problems and how you handled them as evidence.
